assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson is a clear, concrete discovery that completed the Standard Model's particle content and confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical prediction; the experimental discovery has not been honoured. The discovery itself is the centre of the case, and its importance and lasting impact are beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was made by two collaborations of several thousand people, so credit must go to those who conceived and led the experiments. The proposed trio are the early proponents and long-time leaders of ATLAS (Jenni) and CMS (Della Negra, Virdee). This is a defensible but imperfect allocation, since the rules and the collaborative character make any three-person configuration contestable, and other leaders (spokespersons at the time of discovery, accelerator and detector pioneers) could be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the discovery was announced in 2012, independently confirmed by two experiments, and properties (spin-parity, couplings) have been measured with growing precision at the LHC. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among the many leaders of ATLAS and CMS and the LHC machine builders is inherently arbitrary; I rely on general knowledge of who founded the projects and have not verified roles in detail.
Whether the committee would prefer to reward the experimental collaborations through named founders rather than through some other configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened an entire field of moire quantum matter. The idea is original and the experimental discovery was surprising and tied to a clear theoretical prediction, which is the kind of discovery-plus-theory pairing I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald theory predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in 2018. These three names give a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others (Cao, Fatemi, Dean, Yacoby, Young and further experimental groups) made important contributions, and the credited list excludes some of them.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the key results were reproduced by many independent groups within a few years and the field has grown rapidly. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity remains debated, which makes it somewhat early, but the discovery of the phenomena is secure.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene is unresolved.
Credit sharing with early experimental co-discoverers (e.g. students and postdocs in the original papers) and other groups is not covered by the supplied names.
Timing may be slightly early compared with more settled topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened a new window on the universe, with the first evidence for a diffuse flux, and later associations with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane and Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068. It is a major experimental discovery with consequences for the origin of cosmic rays.
assessment.attribution: The credited list contains only Francis Halzen, who conceived and led the IceCube project. A single laureate is a clean, though possibly incomplete, attribution; other founders and collaboration leaders could be considered, but no further names are supplied, so the proposal is limited to him.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense that the diffuse flux is firmly established (well above 5 sigma) and confirmed by multiple analyses. Source identification is still developing and neutrino astronomy is still young.
uncertainties: The identification of individual sources is statistically less robust than the existence of the flux.
Allocation of credit for a large collaboration to one person is open to challenge, and I cannot verify the relative roles of other IceCube leaders and predecessors such as DUMAND and AMANDA.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the time-reversal-invariant quantum spin Hall insulator and the subsequent discovery of topological insulators created a broad paradigm in condensed matter physics, linking band topology to protected boundary states. Deep, original and widely influential.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical proposal of the Z2 topological order is due to Kane and Mele; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells (following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, who are not on this list). Hasan is credited for the 3D materials. A prize of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is plausible but leaves out theorists (Bernevig, Zhang, Fu) and experimentalists who share parts of the credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the effect was experimentally confirmed in several systems and the concept has been confirmed repeatedly since 2005-2007, with consequences for the later quantum anomalous Hall effect. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The credit among the theory proposals (Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane-Mele) and the experimental realisations is contested.
The candidate is compound and the supplied list may not support a fair split of the whole discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 quantum key distribution founded quantum cryptography and, with the wider programme in quantum information, shows how fundamental quantum features have practical consequences. Original and of lasting impact, and it has been experimentally demonstrated and commercialised.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the authors of the BB84 protocol; Ekert independently proposed an entanglement-based scheme in 1991. The credited list contains two spellings of Ekert's name, which I treat as a single person; I propose only Bennett and Brassard as the clearest originators, leaving Ekert's claim as an unresolved allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the theory (security proofs, experiments over fibres and satellites) although practical deployment and device-level security remain topics of research. The 2022 prize recognised related entanglement experiments, so some of the area has been honoured.
uncertainties: The relation of the prize to the 2022 award for Bell-inequality experiments and quantum information science.
Whether Ekert should share credit with Bennett and Brassard; the credited names include duplicated entries for him.
The question of whether this is physics or computer science in nature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP mapped the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with precision, fixing the age, composition and geometry of the universe and establishing the standard Lambda-CDM model. Its importance to cosmology is large and this is a data-driven discovery of the type that fits the principle of finding clues in nature.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was the principal investigator of WMAP, Page and Spergel were key team members, with Spergel leading much of the cosmological parameter analysis. The team was large, and the three names do not capture every contributor; the COBE prize in 2006 and the Planck follow-up complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: results confirmed and refined by Planck and ground-based experiments. The principal question is whether recognition beyond the 2006 prize for CMB anisotropy and the 2019 cosmology prize is warranted.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 (COBE) and 2019 (Peebles) prizes may reduce the case.
Credit among the large WMAP team and with Planck is difficult to separate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped-ion quantum computation began with the Cirac-Zoller proposal and was realised in experiments demonstrating high-fidelity gates, entanglement and quantum simulation. A foundation of quantum information processing with substantial lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the gate scheme in 1995; Blatt led experiments realising entangling gates and large-scale entangled states with ions. Others (Wineland, Monroe, who share a related earlier prize or claims) are not on this list, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of many independent demonstrations, and the 2012 prize recognised ion manipulation. The area is still evolving into scalable computing, so a prize may be considered slightly early or overlapping with other quantum computing awards.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Wineland prize and the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.
The omission of Monroe, Wineland and others from the credited names affects the fairness of the configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres created a versatile platform for nanoscale quantum sensing and quantum information in a solid. The technique is original and has a wide range of uses in physics, materials science and biology.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first optical detection of single NV spins and their coherent control; Lukin contributed major work on NV-based quantum registers and sensing. The three names provide a reasonable trio, though other groups (Awschalom, Hanson, Yacoby, Wrachtrup's collaborators) have claims and the field overlaps with candidate B033.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: reproducible across many groups and widely used, but the sensing and network applications continue to develop, so the recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Credit overlaps with other solid-state spin qubit work and the optical interface candidate.
It is not clear how far the technology has delivered a decisive scientific discovery as opposed to a technique.
